steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease 2 large cookie sheets with vegetable shortening.

Cream the butter and sugars together in a large bowl. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until well blended. Sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt; gradually blend into the batter. Stir in the chopped macadamia nuts and chocolate chips. Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto the cookie sheets, about 2 inches apart.
Bake in preheated oven for 10 to 12 minutes, or until the cookies are golden brown. Remove from the oven, and transfer the cookies to cooling racks.

review.reviewBody: The cookies are delicious & easy. However, I could not add all the chips & nuts to this little bit of dough. I have already made a note on my recipe card to double the dough for the amount of nuts & chips. I got 2 dozen cookies - 2-2 1/2" in diameter.

OK, The first batch was a disater! 375 degrees burnt the cookies and dried them out at 7 minutes. So i gave it a second try with some changes. Cooked at 350 degrees for 6 minutes on parchment paper no greasing the pan as other reviews reccomend. 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips, 1 1/2 cup of flour as the first batch had to many nuts falling out, lastly 1/2 teaspoon Almond Extract. End result GREAT COOKIES! My mom said I should sell them she loved them so much. I don't like chocolate but these were great. Please try them with these modifacations.
I reduced the amount of chips and nuts to 3/4 cup each. Produced a yummy cookie with good ratio of dough to chips/nuts. Toasted the nuts beforehand - 350 degrees, 12 minutes.

I read the other reviews and split the teaspoon of vanilla extract. Instead I added 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla extract and 1/2 teaspoon of almond extract. I, personally, like the way macadamia nuts taste with white chocolate, bu because white chocolate is so sweet; I also added dark chocolate chips. This recipe is also very good as written. I used a toaster oven, and needed to dial back the heat to 350 degrees.

I made these cookies twice. The first time I made a half batch and used only 1 yolk instead of 1/2 egg. It came out perfect. I didn't measure the amount of nuts and chocolate the first time I tried, just eyeball. It only make 9 cookies from half a batch though. The second time, I followed everything, but I couldn't add the same amount of nuts and chocolates as they were impossible to add all of them! I used about 1 cup of each and they were still to much. I will suggest using only 1/3-1/2 cup next time. The taste is so good and the texture is right. I will definitely make these again and USE LESS NUTS AND CHOCOLATE CHIPS! (That's why I give it 4 stars!) I baked mine for only 7-8 minutes and took them out when they were slightly undercooked. For someone who has trouble of burning them, I will suggest to CHECK THE COOKIES AT 7 MINUTES and watch them closely after that. They came out perfect and stay soft the next days! Thanks a lot. ;-D NOTE: It only make about 18-20 cookies for 1 batch!!!

Very tasty, quick and easy, great recipe! 
I used a little less sugar. We don't eat many sweet things. 
I also added a 1/4 tsp of baking soda, it turned out to be nice and fluffy.
I consider Macadamia seeds to be the best "nut."

I am unsure how people can give rating less than 5. I followed the recipe, no substitutions (people who complain about the recipe after changing ingredients blows my mind). Anywho's, my husband and I loved them. The batch I made lasted about three days, I will need to make more. Simply delicious!! This recipe is simple to follow - I would however, keep an eye on the people who provided tips -like putting the batter in the refrigerator, whipping the butter and sugar until just blended, etc.

I don't like nuts in my cookies, but it was my friend's birthday and his favorite cookies are macadamia chocolate chip... so I thought I'd give these a try. Uhhh... they were delicious. :o) Probably the ONLY cookies with nuts that I actually really enjoyed in my lifetime. I also didn't grease my cookie sheet... the stick of butter called for in the recipe will naturally grease it for you! ;o) I didn't have time to wait for the butter to soften, so I just roughly mashed it up with the sugar, then used an old-fashioned blender from the 80s to beat in the egg and vanilla (I used 1 1/2 tsp of vanilla) until pretty smooth. I added some roughly crushed macadamias along with whole ones, semisweet chocolate chips, and dropped them by rounded tablespoonfuls instead of teaspoonfuls for bigger cookies. Yummy!! Oh, and I baked for only 6 minutes... my oven must be powerful... hehe. My friend LOVED them...! Thanks for the recipe! :o)

These cookies were delicious; I've made them twice. The second time I used parchment paper instead of oiling the cookie sheet which eliminated the oily taste of the first batch. The second batch I used semisweet special dark chocolate morsels and pecans instead of macadamia nuts, and they were perfect. The recipe was easily adaptable to the new ingredients.

I reduced the white chips to 1cup and that was perfect for us. I didn't grease the pan and I was careful to not let the cookie get too brown otherwise they were pretty crispy. Pull them out when the edges just begin to brown, let them sit on the pan for another minute so they won't be too soft on the cooling rack. Wonderful cookie, I'll be sure to use this recipe again.
I accidentally put the flour in with the butter & dry ingredients. Then I added the rest. No sifting. They turned out great!
Added cinimon

Do not. I repeat DO NOT only use the amount of flour called for in this recipe. If you measure your flour like most, by scooping it in and leveling it off, you will get the thinnest most sugary cookie of all time. If you measure your flour as I do, by spooning it in the measuring cup and leveling it off, you need an additional 1/2 cup of flour to get it to not spread and have texture.
Turned out great! Added 1 1/3 cup flour. 1/2 cup macadamia chopped 1/4 cup mini semi sweet chocolate morsels. Was the taste I was looking for!

The perfect soft cookie recipe that is not overly sweet and elevates the combo of chocolate and macadamia. I am not a huge chocolate fan so I added only about 1/2 cup of chocolate chips. Watch closely while baking because they brown up quickly at 375 degrees. A new favorite that is quick and easy to make. They will be a staple at every family gathering from now on.
Easy to make. Adjust nuts as prefered.i add 2 tbsp of rolled oats and 1tbsp of cocoa powder to darken the color.like from starbucks. :-)
The only thing I did differently was lining the cookie sheet with parchment paper and refrigerating the dough for about 20 minutes before baking. Perfect cookie. thanks for the recipe!
The recipe has great basev and a classic taste appeal. I find that these are not as sweet as the white chocolate varieties.
Easy to do and so delicious 😌
I loved it ! Turned out yummy! Very easy to make and they wont last very long!
